causal.assumptions_right: CAD was and remains cheap on the 1y z. Brent 105.28 is a genuine terms-of-trade support. Cash BoC at 2.30 versus SOFR 3.90 is a large policy gap.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Mapped REER cheapness onto the claim that the 2Y spread was too wide and must compress. At 140.25 the 2Y was too tight versus the 160bp cash gap, so the value sign in rates was the opposite of the pack.
causal.causal_divergence: FX cheapness and STIR-spread richness are not the same object. Oil and the USDCAD z argued for CAD, not for compression from an already-tight 140bp 2Y. The pack lost because 140bp mean-reverted toward 160bp cash.
causal.future_implication: Cross-market STIR is rich or cheap versus the cash policy gap first. If 2Y is already aligned with cash, residual CAD value lives in spot. Do not recycle the closed pack while 158bp tracks 160bp.
causal.observed_reality: The quoted spread moved 140.25 to 148.25 in three days, toward cash SOFR 3.90 minus CORRA 2.30 at 160bp, and the long pack was closed at a loss. Frozen forwards now print H7 4.705 versus Mar27 3.125, 158bp, i.e. the tightness has normalized to cash.
causal.original_belief: CAD cheapness plus high oil would force the 2Y US-Canada differential to compress, so a long in SOFR-CORRA_2Y_2027H1 at 140.25 was a valuation convergence trade.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With the same cash 160bp versus a 140bp 2Y print, the rates-value trade was to be long the rate spread, or to skip rates and hold the CAD cheapness in spot USDCAD. The long pack was the wrong sign on the only rates dislocation that then existed.

items.expression_assessment: Long SOFR-CORRA_2Y_2027H1 translated a spot valuation view into a rate-spread short at a print that was already tight to cash.
items.future_rule: If the 2Y SOFR-CORRA minus cash SOFR-CORRA gap is negligible, do not express CAD valuation in SOFR-CORRA packs; the residual, if any, is spot.
items.lesson: A 2Y cross-market spread is not cheap because the currency is cheap. Screen the spread against cash before invoking REER.
items.thesis_assessment: CAD-cheap versus oil remains intact. The rates-compression overlay was the error.
items.timing_assessment: A three-day hold cannot adjudicate CAD valuation; it can only adjudicate whether 140bp was tight to 160bp cash.
items.what_failed: Expression sign versus the cash-forward gap; using 2027H1 STIR as a REER vehicle.
items.what_worked: Cutting the pack once 140bp started normalizing toward cash, rather than adding.

causal.assumptions_right: A yield-gap thesis belongs in a rates cross rather than in an improvised spot substitute, and flattening at the last valid mark avoided inventing a New Zealand level.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: Continuous markability of the New Zealand 10-year leg was treated as given rather than as a binding constraint on a warehoused value expression.
causal.causal_divergence: The spread and result did not move because the market could not be marked, not because the valuation gap closed or the thesis was falsified at a new print.
causal.future_implication: Keep New Zealand closed while the 10-year leg is unmarkable; do not force a substitute tenor or spot residual without a fresh valuation anchor.
causal.observed_reality: The New Zealand 10-year input became unavailable, the spread could not be marked, and the line was flattened at the unchanged minus-23 mark with zero realized result.
causal.original_belief: The New Zealand versus United States 10-year short at minus 23 basis points was a slow-convergence value dislocation worth holding in rates.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: Given unmarkability, the same flatten at the last valid mark would still be taken; holding or rotating into an unanchored New Zealand or Australian substitute would be the error.

items.expression_assessment: Ten-year cross-market is the right home for a slow New Zealand versus United States real-yield dislocation, but it is unusable when one leg is unmarkable and New Zealand new risk is blocked.

facts.invalidation: NZ minus US 10-year follows the 3 August 2022 analog and cheapens another 20 basis points or more from minus 23, or New Zealand labor stays cool enough that a durable New Zealand discount versus the United States becomes the fair 10-year gap.

items.no_new_lesson: A flatten at an unchanged mark with zero realized result is bounded operational variance from an unmarkable New Zealand leg; the process of not warehousing unmarkable New Zealand risk remains sound.
items.sizing_assessment: Flattening a single unmarkable line to zero at unchanged marks shows no sizing error in the outcome; residual risk is now none.
items.thesis_assessment: The New Zealand versus United States 10-year short was a relative-value convergence expression whose economic content was not observed; a flat exit at the unchanged mark leaves the thesis neither proven nor disproven.
items.timing_assessment: The exit was forced by mark integrity, not by a valuation clock or a convergence signal.
items.what_failed: The chosen expression could not survive a single session of missing New Zealand marks, so the valuation thesis was never tested.
items.what_worked: The book was flattened at the last valid mark instead of substituting an invented New Zealand 10-year or rolling the idea into a different unanchored New Zealand dollar expression.
